semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {هَلْ أَتَاكَ}: it is a question in its proper sense, and the rhetoricians call it "arousing interest" (al-tashwīq). It has also been said: it means «قد». The explanation of this was given at {هَلْ أتى عَلَى الإنسان} [al-Insān: 1].

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ}: its parallel was discussed in al-Qiyāma and al-Nāziʿāt. The tanwīn in «يومئذٍ» compensates for a clause indicated by the active participle in «الغاشية», its implied form being: "on the day when it overwhelms people", since no explicitly stated clause precedes it. «خاشعة» and what follows it are ṣifas (adjectives), and «تَصْلى» is the khabar (predicate). Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr read «تَصْلَى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, in the passive; the rest read it with fatḥa, in the active. On both readings the pronoun refers to the faces. Abū Rajāʾ read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the ṣād and doubling of the lām. The meaning of all of this was given in al-Inshiqāq and al-Nisāʾ.
Ibn Kathīr in one transmission, and Ibn Muḥayṣin, read «عاملةً ناصبةً» in the accusative: either as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or by way of censure (dhamm).

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {آنِيَةٍ}: a ṣifa (adjective) of «عَيْنٍ», i.e. hot — whose heat has reached the utmost degree — as in his saying {وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ} [al-Raḥmān: 44]. Hishām read it with imāla, because the alif is not converted from anything else but is original in itself. This is unlike «آنِيَة» in Sūrat al-Insān, for the alif there replaces a hamza, since it is the plural of ināʾ (vessel). So its pattern here is fāʿila, and there afʿila: the wording is the same, while the morphology differs. This is one of the beauties of the science of morphology.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {ضَرِيعٍ}: it is a tree in the Fire. It has also been said: stones. It has also been said: it is the zaqqūm. Abū Ḥanīfa [Translator's note: evidently Abū Ḥanīfa al-Dīnawarī, the author on plants] said: "It is al-shibriq, a bad pasture on which grazing animals put on neither fat nor flesh. Al-Hudhalī said:
4553 - وحُبِسْنَ في هَزْمِ الضَّريعِ فكلُّها ... حَدْباءُ دامِيَةُ الضُّلوعِ حَرُوْدُ
(They were confined among the broken stalks of ḍarīʿ, so that every one of them is hump-backed, with bleeding ribs, giving little milk.)
And Abū Dhuʾayb said:
4554 - رَعَى الشِّبْرِقٌ الريَّانَ حتى إذا ذَوَى ... وعادَ ضَريعاً نازَعَتْه النَّحائِصُ
(He grazed the juicy shibriq until, when it withered and became ḍarīʿ, the barren she-asses contended with him for it.)"
It has also been said: it is the dry ʿarfaj plant when it has broken up. Al-Khalīl said: "[It is] a green, foul-smelling plant which the sea casts up." It has also been said: a plant resembling the boxthorn (ʿawsaj). Al-ḍarāʿa — abasement and humbleness — is from that.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يُسْمِنُ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is in the position of the nominative or the genitive, as describing «طعام» or «ضريع»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for its describing «ضريع», that is valid, because it is affirmed, and fattening and sufficing against hunger are negated of it. But its being nominative as describing «طعام» is not valid, because «طعام» is negated and «يُسْمِنُ» is negated, so its construction is not valid; for the implied form would become: 'they have no food that does not fatten nor suffice against hunger (jamʿ) [Translator's note: so in the text, evidently for «جوع»] except from ḍarīʿ', so the meaning would become: they have food that fattens and suffices against hunger, except from something other than ḍarīʿ — just as you say: 'Zayd has no property that is not of benefit except from ʿAmr's property', whose meaning is that he has property of benefit other than ʿAmr's property." I say: this objection does not hold, because, granting the doctrine of implied meaning (mafhūm), something prevents it here, namely the context; and not every implied meaning is acted upon. As for the example he compared it with, it is correct, but nothing prevents [the implied meaning] there, as the context does in the noble verse. Then the Shaykh said: "If it were said that the clause is in the position of the nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of the omitted noun implied in «إلاَّ مِنْ ضريعٍ», it would be correct, because that is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the noun of laysa, i.e. they have no food except something from ḍarīʿ — or except food from ḍarīʿ — that neither fattens nor suffices against hunger. This is a correct construction and a clear meaning."
Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "Or what is intended is that they have no food at all, because ḍarīʿ is not food even for beasts, let alone for humans; for food is what satisfies or fattens, and it is far from both — as you say: 'so-and-so has no shade except the sun', meaning to negate shade emphatically." The Shaykh said: "On this view it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), since what is from ḍarīʿ does not fall under the word «طعام», as it is not food; but the evident view is that it is connected (muttaṣil), here and in his saying {وَلاَ طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 36]." I say: on al-Zamakhsharī's view given above it does not have to be disconnected, since what is meant is negating the thing together with its proof, i.e. if they have any food, it is nothing but this, which no one counts as food; and like it is "he has no shade except the sun". The verification of this was given at his saying {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الموت إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} [al-Dukhān: 56], and [at the poet's] saying:
4555 - ولا عَيْبَ فيهم غيرَ أنَّ سيوفَهُمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(There is no fault in them except that their swords …)
And the like of it is plentiful.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {لاَّ تَسْمَعُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with the yāʾ dotted below, with ḍamma, in the passive, with «لاغِيةٌ» in the nominative because it stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). Nāfiʿ read likewise, except with the tāʾ dotted above; the masculine and the feminine are both clear, because the feminine gender is metaphorical. The rest read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ dotted above and «لاغيةً» in the accusative; the tāʾ may then be for address, i.e. "you do not hear", or for the feminine, i.e. "the faces do not hear". Al-Mufaḍḍal and al-Jaḥdarī read «لا يَسْمَعُ» with the yāʾ of the absent person, with fatḥa, and «لاغيةً» in the accusative, i.e. no one hears therein.
«لاغِيَة» may be a ṣifa (adjective) of [an implied] "word", in the sense of relation (nasab), i.e. possessing idle talk, or by ascribing idle talk to it figuratively; it may be a ṣifa of [an implied] "group", i.e. an idly talking group; or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-ʿāfiya and al-ʿāqiba, as in his saying {لاَ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً وَلاَ تَأْثِيماً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 25].

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {وَنَمَارِقُ}: plural of numruqa, which is a cushion. She said:
4556 - نحن بَناتِ طارِقْ ... نَمْشي على النَّمَارِقْ
(We are the daughters of Ṭāriq; we walk upon cushions.)
And Zuhayr said:
4557 - كُهولاً وشُبَّاناً حِسانٌ وجوهُهُمْ ... لهم سُرُرٌ مَصْفوفةٌ ونَمارِقْ
(Mature men and youths, handsome of face; they have couches set in rows, and cushions.)
Al-numruqa, with ḍamma on the nūn and the rāʾ, or with kasra on both: two dialectal forms, the more widespread being the first.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {وَزَرَابِيُّ}: plural of zarība, with fatḥa or kasra on the zāy — two well-known dialectal forms. They are broad carpets. It has also been said: those of them which have a pile. «مَبْثوثة» means: spread about.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {الإبل}: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) whose singular is baʿīr, nāqa and jamal. It is feminine, and therefore the feminine tāʾ enters it when it is made diminutive, so one says: ubayla. Its plural is ābāl. They derived [words] from its form, saying "taʾabbala Zayd", i.e. his camels became many; and they expressed wonder from it, saying "mā ābalahu", i.e. how many camels he has! It was discussed in al-Anʿām.
His saying: {كَيْفَ}: accusative through «خُلِقَتْ», in the same way as it is accusative in his saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28]. The clause is a badal (substitute) from «الإِبل», a badal of inclusion (ishtimāl), so it is in the position of the genitive; in reality it suspends (tuʿalliq) the looking. «إلى» has entered upon «كيف» in their saying "look at how he does it" (unẓur ilā kayfa yaṣnaʿu). A clause containing an interrogative may be substituted for a noun containing no interrogative, as in their saying: "I came to know Zayd — whose father is he?" — on which there is a disagreement established in the science of grammar.
The majority read «خُلِقَتْ», «رفِعَتْ», «نُصِبَتْ» and «سُطِحَتْ» in the passive, with the tāʾ quiescent for the feminine. The Commander of the Faithful [ʿAlī], Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Ḥaywa read «خَلَقْتُ» and what follows it with the tāʾ of the first person, in the active. The majority read «سُطِحَتْ» undoubled, and al-Ḥasan with doubling.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {بِمُصَيْطِرٍ}: the majority read it with ṣād; Qunbul in some of his chains, and Hishām, with sīn; Khalaf with the ṣād given a hint (ishmām) of zāy, without disagreement; and from Khallād there are two ways. Hārūn read «بمُسَيْطَرٍ» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, as a passive participle, because «سَيْطَرَ» is transitive in their usage, as shown by the verb that is its reflexive (muṭāwiʿ), tasayṭara. No active participle on the pattern mufayʿil has occurred except musayṭir, mubayqir, muhaymin and mubayṭir, from sayṭara, bayqara, haymana and bayṭara. Mujaymir has occurred as the name of a valley, and mudaybir. It has been said: their originals may be «مُجْمِر» and «مُدْبِر», made diminutive. I say: it was mentioned to you before that some allowed «مُهَيْمِناً» to be a diminutive, and it was mentioned that this is a grave error; that was in Sūrat al-Māʾida and elsewhere.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن تولى}: the majority read «إلاَّ» as a particle of exception, and there are two views on it. First: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because it is excepted from the pronoun of «عليهم». Second: it is connected (muttaṣil), because it is excepted from the object of «فَذَكِّرْ», i.e. so remind My servants, except whoever turns away. It has also been said: «مَنْ» is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun of «عليهم»; Makkī said this. This is not possible according to the Ḥijāzīs unless it is connected; if it is disconnected, it is permissible according to Tamīm, because they treat it like the connected; and in the connected, following [the case of the preceding noun] (itbāʿ) is preferred because [the sentence] is not affirmative. All of this applies when «مَنْ تولَّى» is not made a condition with what follows as its apodosis; if you make it so, it is disconnected; its verification was given before. On the view that it is excepted from the implied object of «فَذَكِّرْ», the negative clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ).
Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Aslam and Qatāda read «ألا» as an opening particle (ḥarf istiftāḥ), followed by a conditional clause or a relative noun that includes its meaning.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِيَابَهُمْ}: the majority read it with the yāʾ undoubled, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of āba yaʾūbu iyāban [the original being awaba yaʾwubu iwāban], i.e. he returned, like qāma yaqūmu qiyāman. Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar read it with the yāʾ doubled. The views of the morphologists on it are in confusion. It has been said: it is the maṣdar of ayyaba, on the pattern fayʿala like bayṭara; one says from it: ayyaba yuʾayyibu iyyāban. The original is aywaba yuʾaywibu iywāban, like bayṭara yubayṭiru; the yāʾ and the wāw came together in all of that, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the added yāʾ was assimilated into it; so iyyāb on this view is fīʿāl. It has also been said: rather it is the maṣdar of awwaba on the pattern fawʿala like ḥawqala, the original being iwwāb with two wāws, the first added and the second the middle radical of the word; the first was quiescent after a kasra, so it was changed to yāʾ, giving iywāban; then a yāʾ and a wāw came together, the first quiescent, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ after it; so its pattern is fīʿāl, like ḥīqāl, whose original is ḥiwqāl. It has also been said: rather it is the maṣdar of awwaba on the pattern faʿwala like jahwara, the original being iwwāb on the pattern fiʿwāl like «جِهْوار», the first [wāw] being the middle radical and the second added; and the same was done to it as was done to the preceding one, of conversion and assimilation, for the reasons given before, which are understood from what has passed. If it is said: assimilation prevents changing the wāw to yāʾ — it is answered: it prevents it only when the wāw and the yāʾ are the middle radical, and you have learned that the yāʾ in fayʿal and the wāw in fawʿal and faʿwal are added. It has also been said: rather it is the maṣdar of awwaba on the pattern faʿʿala, like kidhdhāban; the original is iwwāb, then the first wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, so one said: iywāban. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like dīwān from diwwān; then the same was done to it as was done to sayyid" — he means that its original is saywid, so it was converted and assimilated. Abū al-Faḍl [Translator's note: the text has «أو بالفضل», evidently for «أبو الفضل»] also inclined to this.
However, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected what the two of them said, on the ground that they [the grammarians] stated explicitly that a wāw originally formed as doubled (assimilated) does not have its first [element] changed to yāʾ, even if what precedes it has kasra. He said: "And they exemplified this with this very word «إوَّاب», the maṣdar of the doubled awwaba, and with ikhriwwāṭ, the maṣdar of ikhrawwaṭa." He said: "As for al-Zamakhsharī's comparison with dīwān, it is not good, because they never pronounced it assimilated in its original form, and they did not say diwwān; were it not for the plural dawāwīn, it would not be known that the origin of this yāʾ is wāw. And they stated explicitly that «دِيْوان» is irregular (shādhdh), so nothing else is to be analogised on it."
I say: as for their not having pronounced diwwān, it does not follow from that that what al-Zamakhsharī said is to be rejected. The grammarians stated explicitly that the original of «دِيْوان» is diwwān, and of «قيراط», qirrāṭ, as shown by the plurals dawāwīn and qarārīṭ. Its being irregular does not detract, because he did not mention it as something on which to analogise, but as a comparison.
Makkī went towards something like this, saying: "The origin of the yāʾ is wāw, but it changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it. Whoever reads with doubling ought to have said: iwwābahum, since it is from the wāw; or to have said: iywābahum, replacing the first of the doubled letters with yāʾ, as they said «دِيْوان», the original being diwwān." End of quote.
It has also been said: it is the maṣdar of aʾwaba, on the pattern akrama, from al-awb (return); the original is iʾwāb, like ikrām; the second hamza of iʾwāb was replaced with yāʾ because it was quiescent after a hamza with kasra, so the word became iywāban; then the yāʾ and the wāw came together as described before, so it was converted and assimilated; its pattern is ifʿāl. This is clear.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said about this view: "The hamza was softened, and what was due in assimilation was to make it iwwāban, but the yāʾ was preferred in it, contrary to analogy." End of quote. This is not good, since you have learned that once the hamza was changed to yāʾ, analogy requires doing what was described before, changing the wāw to yāʾ, not the reverse. I have only set out these views with explanation because of their difficulty, together with the lack of anyone among the parsers who examines closely such unsettled places of rare usage. He put the khabar (predicate) first in his saying «إلينا» and «علينا» to intensify the severity and the threat.
